newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa gains strength after heart surgery.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa gains strength after heart surgery.

text.p: Mother Teresa gained strength on Thursday after life-saving heart surgery but was not out of danger, doctors and officials at an Indian heart clinic said.
"Mother Teresa's condition is improving," doctors treating the 86-year-old Roman Catholic nun at Calcutta's B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre said in a regular morning bulletin.
The bulletin described the 1979 Nobel Peace prize winner as "looking fresh" but said she was still not out of danger after surgery on Friday to clear two coronary artery blockages.
It said Mother Teresa, who on Wednesday took her first steps since the operation with help from clinic staff, had a good sleep.
"She is cheerful," clinic administrator S.K. Tiwari told Reuters.
He said Mother Teresa, who has devoted her life to the poor, destitute and dying, sat in a chair and said prayers after taking morning tea.
Mother Teresa's post-operative condition was complicated by an irregular heartbeat, bronchial pneumonia and long-standing kidney and lung problems.
Last Friday marked her third round of heart-related surgery in five years.
Doctors said they were hoping to release Mother Teresa by the weekend. But Thursday's bulletin said: "She is still not out of danger."
Clinic administrator A.K. Chatterjee said: "Everything is now under control and we are optimistic."
Doctors believe recovery will take a long time and Mother Teresa, who was fitted with a heart pacemaker in 1989, may never be as active as before.
Dr Tarun Praharaj, a member of her medical panel, said she was impatient to leave hospital and get back to her work with the poor.
"I'm quite strong. I want to go home," he quoted her as saying on Wednesday.
Despite numerous health problems, Mother Teresa had kept up a tireless pace as head of her Missionaries of Charity religious order and travelled widely.
The order runs 456 homes in 111 countries.
